Galba -
Don't give me the name!
He was right when the beast strangled him!
He betrayed the friend!
then I feel his kiss glow -
My lips are still burning hot with shame and shame.
Mistress, Myrtocle -
What do you want?
Galba didn't come alone -
I only saw him -
And him who strangled him,
Yes - an adverse animal -
O Mistress - Mistress - still! - It was Arcesius, was your husband!
You fool! - This beast that escaped Hades himself,
this monster, limping, disfiguring. - this is Arcesius? -
You're foolish!!
It was him, Mistress, who was Arcesius.
Have mercy, great gods!
Myrtocle -
- Shut up!
Amor and psyche, o lost dream!
So the fairytale lied:
It wasn't Amor who found Psyche's little lamp.
It was a monster, and all lies all around,
In a sea of lies I find blind!
Mistress, Myrtocle -
- Why didn't you tell me?
That my luck was just a lie?
She was all your luck, was Arcesius's luck!
And so it was - why did you let me go to the man,
who gave me the light - which shattered my happiness?
You're begging!
And this man raised his hand - I saw -
and all happiness lay in shards! -
He's cursed!
Don't think about him!
No, no, no!
Is it his fault you see now?
Leave me alone!
He loved you so much!
Arcesius -
Smash his luck is even more like yours!
What he did, he did everything for you!
O how I love him,
as only my ear drank his voice sound!
It's not too late yet -
Not too late!
Leave me alone, Arsinoe - I want to be alone!
I'm leaving, Mistress.
O was I still the ignorant blind child,
at the Isthmos beach - under the olive trees -
How was it?
"You have to give up your own happiness,
to save the others!" -
Yes - so it was! - Renunciation is the virtue of the suffering -
Sacrifice his happiness - sacrifice himself - for his neighbor -
this is the man's teaching that gave me the light -
Isn't Arcesius my neighbor?
Happy was he, happy was I when I was blind -
And all misfortune brought the light -
So let the sun burn out again my eyes light!
Stand wide open, my eyes,
Don't weep, my eyes!
May the Phoibo's arrows hit you,
may they sink your pride into eternal night!
O my dear dead eyes -
Myrtocle - Myrtocle -
Finally - finally! - I hear your voice -
Where are you - I don't see you -
You don't see me - you don't see me?
I don't see you - but I hear your word.
And so fine is my ear that your steps rhythm
quietly trembling in my heart -
You don't see anymore?
No, I don't know how it happened.
I looked to the sun and the light went out!
And I'm grateful that I'm blind again.
You don't see me?
- I never saw you!
- Who did you see?
I saw Arsinoe - saw Jesus -
Did you see Galba?
Yes, I saw him -
And did you see the one who attacked him?
- I don't know who did it.
And me, you didn't see me?
No! No!
O why dost thou torment me, my beloved Lord,
You Iris of my dead eyes, you?
I saw so much, so much - only you alone I don't see! -
And I'll never see you!
But I want to live on in the dream world
for you, beloved husband, for you alone!
Myrtocle - Myrtocle - beloved woman -
Your voice sound engulfs me
like a warm rain in May -
Myrtocle, Myrtocle, beloved woman -
Your finger pressure engulfs me
like a soft coat at the bathroom -
Myrtocle -
in the story of Mary of Magdala.
"Rejoice with me, for I have found my sheep that was lost!" etc.
The curtain falls slowly
